subject: Green Score and Incentive Zoning Frameworks
overview: The committee discussed frameworks for a new environmental 'green score' and an incentive zoning program to trade increased density for community benefits like affordable housing. The body directed staff to prepare draft language for both programs to be reviewed alongside upcoming corridor rezoning plans.

items.title: Green Score and Heat Mitigation
items.summary: The committee reached a consensus to implement a 100-point green score metric focused on heat mitigation and functional landscapes for projects triggering site plan review. Staff were directed to coordinate with the Engineering Department to ensure the new rubric does not conflict with existing stormwater regulations.

items.title: Incentive Zoning Models
items.summary: Members reviewed incentive zoning models from other cities and expressed a preference for a simplified system that grants height bonuses in exchange for affordable housing, ground-floor commercial space, and transit improvements. The program will primarily target development in squares and high-density corridors like Mystic Avenue.

items.title: Condominium Conversion Status
items.summary: Staff clarified that condominium conversion regulations are classified as city ordinances rather than zoning by-laws.

items.title: Housing Definitions
items.summary: The committee reviewed comparative definitions for residential types including co-living, congregate housing, and single-room occupancy to align Medford’s code with modern housing models. Councilors requested that the new definitions avoid overly restrictive language regarding the number of unrelated individuals living together.
